correctness.rationale: The order-n<=8 theorem is finite and is genuinely established by full exhaustive enumeration modulo plant row permutations: every nonzero plant-neighborhood incidence row is drawn with repetition from 1..2^b-1 for all a+b<=8, connected initial graphs filtered, every survivor mask considered, component order computed, pairs compared within exact sorted plant/pollinator degree signatures. An independent implementation used BFS rather than the package DSU and reproduced connected profiles 1,2,5,18,89,590,5160; signature counts 1,2,4,10,27,80,241; distinct vectors 1,2,4,10,27,85,285; 55 unequal-vector comparisons, all componentwise ordered. Direct independent nine-witness enumeration gave A(G)=(1,14,40,59,40,9), A(H)=(1,14,41,58,38,9); their difference expands q(1-q)^2(2-3q). Distinct independent set-DP computed max matching equal for all 32 surviving pollinator sets. This is exhaustive only through eight vertices, not a theorem for arbitrary order.
